title: Faithful flatness of a finitely generated commutative Hopf subalgebra inclusion
statement: Let $k$ be a field [def-weil-field]. A commutative Hopf $k$-algebra here means a unital commutative $k$-algebra $A$ with $k$-algebra maps $\Delta_A:A\to A\otimes_k A$, $\epsilon_A:A\to k$, $S_A:A\to A$ such that $(\Delta_A\otimes1)\Delta_A=(1\otimes\Delta_A)\Delta_A$, $(\epsilon_A\otimes1)\Delta_A=(1\otimes\epsilon_A)\Delta_A=1_A$, and $\mu_A(S_A\otimes1)\Delta_A=\mu_A(1\otimes S_A)\Delta_A=\eta_A\epsilon_A$, under the usual tensor unit and associativity identifications; $\mu_A$ and $\eta_A$ are multiplication and unit. Tensor products are those of [lem-weil-pbc-algebra-tensor-pushout-universal-property]. Let $A,B$ be commutative Hopf $k$-algebras, each finitely generated as a $k$-algebra [def-weil-pbc-finite-type-algebra]. Let $i:A\to B$ be an injective $k$-algebra homomorphism satisfying $\Delta_Bi=(i\otimes i)\Delta_A$, $\epsilon_Bi=\epsilon_A$, and $S_Bi=iS_A$. Then $B$ is a faithfully flat $A$-module through $i$ [def-weil-pbc-faithfully-flat-ring-map]. No reducedness, perfectness, smoothness, cocommutativity or characteristic hypothesis is imposed.

source.place: Theorem 3.31, printed pp.73--74; Definition 3.3, printed pp.65--66, and Definition 3.8, printed p.67, for the commutative Hopf algebra convention.

proof.text: Choose an algebraic closure $K/k$ [def-weil-algebraic-closure]. Put $A_K=A\otimes_kK$ and $B_K=B\otimes_kK$. The maps $A\to A_K$, $B\to B_K$ are faithfully flat by [lem-weil-pbc-field-extension-base-change-faithfully-flat]. Also $k\to K$ is faithfully flat (apply that node with $D=k$), so [lem-trf-flat-tensor-preserves-injection] makes $i_K=i\otimes1$ injective. Generators of $A,B$ tensored with $1$ generate $A_K,B_K$ over $K$. Extend each Hopf structure map by scalars, using the algebra tensor universal property [lem-weil-pbc-algebra-tensor-pushout-universal-property]; each required identity is the original equality tensored with $K$, so $i_K$ is a Hopf homomorphism. We prove faithful flatness over an algebraically closed field in steps 2--5 and descend it in step 6.

source.place: Theorem 3.31, p.73, reduction to an algebraic closure; scalar-extension details expanded.

proof.text: Now assume $k$ algebraically closed. Apply [lem-sfb-hopf-reduced-core-nilpotent-fibre] to $A$ and choose its finitely generated reduced Hopf subalgebra $C$. Set $C^+=\ker\epsilon_C$, $D=A/(C^+A)$, $E=B/(i(C^+)B)$. In particular the augmentation ideal $D^+=\ker\epsilon_D$ is nilpotent. The composite $C\hookrightarrow A\xrightarrow{i}B$ is injective and Hopf, and $C,B$ are finitely generated over $k$. Hence [lem-sfb-reduced-target-dominant-group-flatness], applied with its domain algebra equal to $C$, makes $C\to B$ faithfully flat. This uses reducedness of $C$ only; it makes no reducedness assumption on $A$ or $B$.

source.place: Theorem 3.31, p.74, reduced Frobenius core H-prime, with 3.23 and 3.29.

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-hopf-relative-kernel-shear] to $C\hookrightarrow A\xrightarrow{i}B$. It gives the Hopf map $\alpha:D\to E$ and the isomorphisms $\Phi_A,\Phi_B$ with $\Phi_B(i\otimes_C1_B)=(\alpha\otimes_k1_B)\Phi_A$. Since $B$ is flat over $C$, [lem-trf-flat-tensor-preserves-injection] applied to the $C$-linear injection $i$ proves $i\otimes_C1_B$ injective. The displayed square therefore makes $\alpha\otimes_k1_B$ injective. The algebra $B$ is nonzero, since its counit sends $1$ to $1\in k$. Choose a $k$-basis of $B$; it is nonempty, and tensoring any $k$-module complex with $B$ gives a nonempty direct sum of copies of that complex, which is exact exactly when the original is exact, coordinate by coordinate. Thus $B$ is faithfully flat over $k$. Now [lem-trf-faithfully-flat-ltensor-injective-reflection], with $R=k$, $S=B$ and $f=\alpha$ (interchanging tensor factors), proves that $\alpha$ is injective.

source.place: Theorem 3.31, p.74, injectivity of a and b and its reflection to O(M) to O(N).

proof.text: The quotients $D,E$ are finitely generated, as the images of finite algebra generating families for $A,B$ still generate their quotients. Their induced Hopf structures and the compatibility of $\alpha$ are part of [lem-sfb-hopf-relative-kernel-shear]. Its domain $D$ has nilpotent augmentation ideal by step 2. Choose a $k$-basis of $E/(\alpha(D^+)E)$ and lifts in $E$. By [lem-sfb-nilpotent-hopf-basis-lifting] these lifts give an isomorphism $E\simeq\bigoplus_J D$ of $D$-modules. The counit of $E$ vanishes on $\alpha(D^+)E$ and sends $1$ to $1$, so this quotient is nonzero and $J$ is nonempty. For every complex of $D$-modules, tensoring with this free module gives a nonempty direct sum of copies; exactness holds if and only if it holds in each coordinate. Thus $\alpha:D\to E$ is faithfully flat in precisely the definition [def-weil-pbc-faithfully-flat-ring-map].

source.place: Theorem 3.31, pp.73--74, using the nilpotent special case only as a stated input; the freeness-to-faithful-flatness argument is written out.

proof.text: By [lem-weil-pbc-faithfully-flat-base-change], the base change $b_i=\alpha\otimes_k1_B:D\otimes_kB\to E\otimes_kB$ is faithfully flat: its codomain is $E\otimes_D(D\otimes_kB)$ under $(e\otimes(d\otimes b))\mapsto e\alpha(d)\otimes b$, with inverse $e\otimes b\mapsto e\otimes(1\otimes b)$. The isomorphisms and commuting square of [lem-sfb-hopf-relative-kernel-shear] transfer this to $a_i=i\otimes_C1_B:A\otimes_CB\to B\otimes_CB$. To descend, put $R=A\otimes_CB$; $A\to R$ is faithfully flat by the same base-change lemma, since $C\to B$ is faithfully flat. For any complex $L$ of $A$-modules there is the canonical associativity isomorphism $R\otimes_A(L\otimes_AB)\simeq(R\otimes_AL)\otimes_R(B\otimes_CB)$. Explicitly the isomorphism sends $(a\otimes b)\otimes(l\otimes x)$ to $((a\otimes b)\otimes l)\otimes(x\otimes1)$; its inverse sends $((a\otimes b)\otimes l)\otimes(x\otimes y)$ to $(a\otimes by)\otimes(l\otimes x)$. Faithful flatness of $A\to R$ and of $a_i$ implies that the right side is exact if and only if $L$ is exact. Faithful flatness of $A\to R$ also says that the left side is exact if and only if $L\otimes_AB$ is exact. Hence $L\otimes_AB$ is exact if and only if $L$ is exact, proving faithful flatness of $i$ [def-weil-pbc-faithfully-flat-ring-map].

source.place: Theorem 3.31, p.74, final faithfully-flat descent, expanded via the exactness definition; Stacks Tags 00HI and 00HB.

proof.text:
Apply steps 2--5 to $i_K$ from step 1. For a complex $L$ of $A$-modules, the scalar-extension isomorphism
$$A_K\otimes_A(L\otimes_AB)\simeq(A_K\otimes_AL)\otimes_{A_K}B_K$$
sends $(a\otimes c)\otimes(l\otimes b)$ to $(al\otimes1)\otimes(b\otimes c)$, Its inverse sends $((a\otimes c)\otimes l)\otimes(b\otimes d)$ to $(a\otimes cd)\otimes(l\otimes b)$; the tensor balancing relations make both maps well defined. The right side is exact if and only if $A_K\otimes_AL$ is exact, by faithful flatness of $i_K$, and this is equivalent to exactness of $L$ by faithful flatness of $A\to A_K$. The left side is exact if and only if $L\otimes_AB$ is exact, again by faithful flatness of $A\to A_K$. These equivalences prove that $i$ is faithfully flat [def-weil-pbc-faithfully-flat-ring-map]. Since the field extension was made only inside this argument, the original arbitrary field and all the stated absence-of-extra-hypotheses clauses are retained.
